trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket probability move is accompanied by any wire headline on US-Vietnam trade talks; if none, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare VNM move versus broad EM ETF (EEM) to isolate Vietnam-specific signal from general risk-on moves.
time_plan.2h: Scan for US Trade Representative or White House statements confirming negotiation progress.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether move persists or fades; check Vietnam-exposed names (NKE, apparel/electronics supply chain) for corroboration.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether VNM held direction into Asia session open; mark whether the 700bps threshold was realistically reached.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a formal US-Vietnam trade agreement would signal easing tariff/trade friction, which directly benefits Vietnam-domiciled exporters and the local market. VNM is the most liquid, direct proxy for Vietnamese equity. However, a 'free trade agreement becoming law' is a very high bar requiring Congressional action, so even a probability spike more likely reflects incremental negotiation progress (e.g., a tariff framework) than imminent legal enactment, dampening the realistic 12h equity move.

evidence_used: Market resolves Yes only if an FTA becomes US law by Dec 31 2026 — a legally demanding, slow-moving condition
US-Vietnam trade/tariff relations have been an active policy theme under the current administration
VNM (VanEck Vietnam ETF) is the primary liquid public-market proxy for Vietnamese equity
uncertainty_notes: The legal bar (law enacted via Congress) is far higher than a negotiated tariff deal, weakening the link between probability moves and near-term asset moves
VNM is thinly traded relative to major ETFs, so moves can be idiosyncratic/illiquid rather than information-driven
A probability move could simply reflect speculative repricing without new public information

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of a US-Vietnam trade deal would most plausibly lift Vietnamese equities via the VNM ETF, reflecting reduced tariff/trade friction. But the resolution criterion (an FTA becoming US law) is a high legal bar, so realistic 12h magnitude is modest and uncertain. This is a weak-to-moderate mapping: direction up, but unlikely to clear the 700bps tradable threshold with confidence.
key_assumptions: Probability moves in this market reflect genuine trade-policy information rather than noise
Easing US-Vietnam trade friction is net positive for Vietnamese exporters/equity
VNM adequately tracks Vietnam-specific sentiment over a 12h window
failure_modes: The news may already be public (tariff frameworks widely reported), so no residual edge in VNM
A 'deal' headline could be a tariff imposition or threat rather than liberalization, reversing the direction
VNM illiquidity and overnight gaps can swamp the signal with idiosyncratic noise
The legal-enactment resolution bar means probability can rise without any near-term fundamental asset catalyst
